input.brief: Solo CG generalist ULTEMA: cinematic full-CGI car commercials for brands and agencies, the whole studio pipeline done by one person

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Film title, bottom edge
hero.blueprint: One photograph fills the viewport at 100vw by 100svh, `object-fit: cover`, with its subject in the upper two-thirds and a calmer, darker zone along the bottom. The name is one condensed uppercase word, or a short name in a high-contrast serif, set at clamp(150px, 17.5vw, 290px) and sized to span the full width between 32px margins. It is centred and anchored so its baseline sits 34px above the bottom edge, covering roughly the lowest quarter of the frame. A soft neutral dark scrim lies under that bottom band only, about 40% of the height; the rest of the image is untouched. Directly above the name's left end, on the same margin, sits the supporting sentence at 16px on two short lines. Directly above its right end, right-aligned, sits the single action as a small paper-coloured rectangular button. The top edge carries a small emblem or wordmark at the left margin and up to five text links at 15px grouped at the right, all in white. The central half of the screen belongs to the view.
hero.mobile: The photograph is re-cropped to portrait with `object-position` on its subject and fills 100svh. The name stays on the bottom edge at 22vw on one line, or two lines at 20vw beyond eight characters, 20px above the edge. The supporting sentence sits above the name's left end at 15px. The action button moves to the top-right corner and the links collapse to a menu word beside the emblem.
hero.headline: The name of the place: one word of up to about 12 characters at 17.5vw, or two words stacked on a phone.

type.note: A wide display sans built from rounded squares, heavy and a little architectural, beside a clean text grotesk. Suits architecture indexes, watches, mobility and events that want a title with a constructed feel.

palette.name: Warm black, gold
palette.note: Warm near-black fills the page and photographs sit bright against it, with pure white small type; panels warm to a brown-black. Gold is for one text link or small button per screen, never a field.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Giant title, uneven wall
sections.blueprint: A one- or two-word title in capitals at clamp(72px, 9vw, 136px), leading 0.9, sits flush left at the 16px margin; on its baseline at the far right, one underlined link at 15px to the full archive. 32px below, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall with 8px gaps: a flex-wrap layout in which each row has a different fixed height (cycle 240, 360, 200, 300px) and each tile's width follows its image ratio, so widths range from one-sixth to one-half of the page and tile edges do not line up between rows. Rows are justified to both margins with `flex-grow`. Under each image, one caption line at 12px: project name left, year in the soft ink right. Square corners; no hover overlay beyond a slight dimming of the other tiles. Holds 9–16 projects. The section ground is one flat colour, dark or saturated, edge to edge.
sections.mobile: Title at 17vw on one line. The wall becomes rows of alternating composition: one full-width tile, then two tiles splitting the width 62/38, then 38/62, with 6px gaps and fixed row heights of 220 and 150px. Captions stay as one line under each tile.

sections.name: Pinned title, portraits pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people. A `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds the heading, two words at clamp(88px, 12vw, 180px), leading 0.85, centred at mid-height, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads over ground and photographs alike. Beneath it in the stacking order, portraits scroll past in normal flow: each a 4:5 photograph 26–30vw wide, alternately starting at column 2 and ending at column 11, 60svh apart, so each one passes behind a different half of the heading. Under each portrait's left corner: the name at 18px, the role at 14px in the soft ink, and one sentence of up to 30 words in a 280px measure. The last portrait is followed by 40svh of empty ground before the heading releases. Square corners. Nothing else is on screen.
sections.mobile: The heading shrinks to 17vw and pins 16px from the top instead of at mid-height. Portraits become 72% wide, alternating between the left and right margins, 48px apart, each with name, role and sentence beneath at the portrait's width.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Kereliott
references.idea: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.
references.hero: Very dark green-black field with cream type. A two-line introductory sentence at about 30px sits top-left inside 30px margins; a small cream rectangular button sits top-right. The upper half is otherwise empty. The house name fills the full content width in a flared humanist sans, mixed case, with capitals about 19vw tall, its baseline at roughly 87% of the viewport height. Immediately beneath, separated by a gap of a few pixels, the top sliver of a full-width landscape photograph enters from the bottom edge.
references.type: A single face, Trust, in regular weight: a humanist sans with flared terminals and old-style figures. The wordmark is an oversized graphic; all other text is one size of about 20-30px plus tiny 10px photo captions. Hierarchy is position, not weight.
references.colour: #161c1a #eae8dc #222926 #1f2926 — Cream on green-black from top to bottom with no accent colour. The map is drawn in a tone barely lighter than the ground, so photographs supply all the colour.
references.imagery: Natural-light photos of a stone cottage, garden and deck with square corners, in mixed portrait and landscape crops at differing sizes. One full-width opener, then small images placed singly with tiny captions under the left corner.
references.layout: 30px margins, text held to the left 60% in one size. Photographs are staggered left and right at different widths with large dark gaps between, like pictures passed on a wall. The name and a booking button stay fixed in the top corners.

sections.description: A full-width landscape photograph runs margin to margin directly under the wordmark, followed after a gap by a four-line paragraph in the single text size, left-aligned and spanning about 85% of the width. There is no heading or label; the text simply continues the sentence begun at the top of the page.

After a left-aligned paragraph, a silhouette map of the region sits centre-left, about half the viewport wide, filled in a green only a few percent lighter than the background. Five towns are marked with small ring dots and tiny labels; only the house's town has a solid cream dot. No border, legend or frame.

Photographs are placed one or two per screen in a stagger: a portrait image about 30% wide against the left margin, a larger near-square one starting lower against the right margin, later a landscape image top-right of centre and a smaller one bottom-left. Each has a 10px caption under its left corner. More than half of every screen is empty dark ground.

Two short left-aligned sentences in the standard text size with underlined inline links to booking platforms and an email address, then a small cream certification badge. The footer is a single line at the very bottom: social link left, copyright centre, three underlined utility links right, with a tall empty gap above.

steal: Size the wordmark to fill the content width exactly and let the first photograph tuck directly under its baseline.
Draw a location map as a tone-on-tone silhouette with one filled dot among ring dots.
Use a single typeface in one weight and essentially one text size, creating hierarchy through placement and emptiness.

references.name: NOTHIN’
references.idea: The studio's name set as a wordmark so large it is the whole hero, repeated in inverted colours as the footer, so 'nothing' is literally the only content on screen.
references.hero: The captured hero frame is a black preloader wipe; this describes the loaded state. White field. A custom heavy geometric wordmark in black spans the full width between 1% margins, vertically centred, about 30% of the viewport tall, its apostrophe hanging at the top-right. Top-left: a two-line statement at about 1.6vw with a small black pill button under it. Top-right: a tiny menu label with a four-dot icon. Along the bottom edge: a one-line studio descriptor at left, two social links and a language chip at right. Everything else is empty white, with no image and no colour.
references.type: PP Neue Montreal medium for statements at up to about 5vw, sentence case, tight tracking and leading; the Book cut for small text; IBM Plex Mono for tiny grey project labels. The wordmark is custom heavy geometric lettering at close to 100vw. Only three text sizes: statement, caption, micro-label.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #2b47e6 #2f5d33 #bfbfbf — Strict black and white that flips by section: white hero and intro, black works and footer. The only colour comes from inside the imagery, chiefly electric-blue foil and fern green.
references.imagery: 3D renders of inflated chrome, crumpled blue foil and bubble-wrap hearts on black; project shots are brand mock-ups photographed in settings (a card among ferns, a laptop on a dark desk). Hard-edged rectangles of varied size, square corners.
references.layout: Margins of about 1%, so content runs nearly edge to edge. The intro is a left headline over a full-width black media panel; the works section places images at irregular widths and horizontal offsets with wide black gaps, each with a mono label and one-line caption above.

sections.description: White section. A two-line statement at about 5vw sits flush left under a small logo mark, filling the top quarter. Below it a black rectangle spans the full content width and runs off the bottom of the viewport, holding a 3D still life clustered at centre. On further scroll the panel shrinks to a small thumbnail docked top-right, while a parenthesised label and a four-line paragraph at caption size appear in two narrow columns at the left.

Black section headed by one bold uppercase word top-left. Project images are placed as a loose scatter: one at about 48% width hugging the left margin, the next narrow and hugging the right margin lower down, the next inset to start 18% across. Above each image sits a tiny grey mono project name, then a one-line white caption at about 1.1vw. A two-line aphorism floats alone at the right between projects. Long stretches of empty black separate items.

Black, full viewport. A two-line invitation at about 5vw at the left in the upper third, with two outlined pill buttons under it; three social links stacked at about 78% across. The wordmark repeats in white at full width, anchored to the bottom, with a single row of micro-text credits beneath it.

steal: Make the hero nothing but the name: a wordmark scaled to the full viewport width on a blank field, with only a two-line statement and one small button in a corner.
Repeat the hero wordmark in inverted colours as the footer so the page opens and closes on the same shape.
Place case-study images at different widths and horizontal offsets on a black field, each with a micro mono label and a single-line caption above it instead of a card.
references.media: No picture on the desktop first screen: a full-width black wordmark on white covers about 30% of the height. Then an inset showreel with 18px gutters scrubs down into a box in the right third as text arrives on the left, a staggered two-column mosaic of 48, 32 and 65% widths, a pinned full-bleed brand film with a blurred copy behind it as a halo, cut-out 3D objects on black with letters tumbling between them, and the wordmark again, inverted, as the footer; 17 images and 4 muted looping videos.
references.motion: The preloader (on the phone capture) morphs a 3D inflatable through three forms while a counter runs down to 000, then white rises in a hard-edged mask to reveal the wordmark. Lenis: the showreel scrubs at 3, works cards drift at their own speeds (y scrub 1.5, yPercent scrub 3), the film pins for one screen, heading letters split and scatter, and services letters and objects tumble in on power2.in at random 0.25-0.69s durations; the house ease is cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) at 0.5-0.6s.

references.name: Jesper Landberg
references.idea: Project screenshots become bent, rippling panels on a horizontal WebGL strip floating above a perspective grid floor in the dark.
references.hero: Black viewport. Four tiny bold uppercase labels sit in the corners with 77px side and 44px vertical margins: name top-left, profile top-right, a view toggle bottom-left, newsletter bottom-right. Across the middle runs a horizontal strip of project panels rendered in WebGL: the centre panel is about 47% of the viewport wide and 52% tall with rounded corners, its top and bottom edges rippling as if the sheet were flexing; neighbours are cropped by the screen edges and angled away. Each panel carries a white project title bottom-left and a round arrow button bottom-right. Below, a white-line perspective grid floor recedes to a dark horizon. The top quarter is empty.
references.type: A single grotesk (digest reports only 'sans'): bold uppercase corner labels at about 11px and project titles at roughly 18 to 27px with tight tracking. No headline at all; the largest type on screen belongs to the project screenshots themselves.
references.colour: #000000 #181818 #373637 #ffffff — Pure black stage with white micro-labels and faint grey grid lines; all colour comes from the project panels, which glow like screens in a dark room.
references.imagery: Website screenshots and videos used as textures on curved, wavy, rounded-corner panels in a 3D scene, with soft vignette shading at panel edges and a wireframe grid floor beneath.
references.layout: A single-screen stage: corner labels frame a horizontal band of panels through the vertical centre, and scroll moves the strip sideways rather than the page down. A toggle switches to a full list. On mobile the projects become a vertical stack of rounded cards.

sections.description: As the strip advances each panel bends differently: the one nearest centre faces the viewer and is largest, panels toward the edges rotate away and shrink, and all share a sine-wave distortion along their top and bottom edges. Gaps between panels are about 10px. Panels whose media has not loaded show as flat pink or starfield fills, still carrying title and arrow button.

On a 390px screen the 3D strip is replaced by a vertical feed: full-width cards with 30px side margins and about 20px radius, each roughly 300px tall, stacked with 30px gaps. The project title sits bottom-left inside the card over a dark gradient scrim, with a black circular arrow button bottom-right. The four corner labels remain fixed over the feed.

steal: Reduce all chrome to four tiny uppercase labels pinned in the corners so the work fills the stage.
Distort carousel panels with a wave tied to scroll velocity so the gallery feels like flexible sheets rather than rigid slides.
Ground a floating gallery with a faint perspective grid floor to give depth on an otherwise black screen.
references.media: One fixed canvas covers the screen and holds about eight project cards on a ring around the camera, each textured with a muted looping screen recording of the site; the cards fill the band from y≈220 to y≈690 edge to edge, the centre one about 670x463 (24% of the area), with neighbours bleeding off both edges over a perspective floor grid. No img or video elements on desktop.
references.motion: A short segmented loader, then the whole ring cuts in by 2.5s with no fly-through (load 844ms). The document does not scroll: the wheel turns the ring about one card per step in an endless loop, as a smooth inertial lerp, and fast steps put an extra wave into the card edges that relaxes when the ring stops; DOM transitions are only .15-.5s on cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1).

notes: type set to unbounded-onest by the owner: gambarino-general has no Cyrillic and the site is EN/RU
